headline: REA Gives Agents Evidence for Reverse Engineering
lede: REA turns reverse engineering into a guided, inspectable workflow for coding agents and terminal users. It connects local tools such as Ghidra, Hopper, Binwalk, and JADX to analyze binaries, applications, firmware, and packages while recording evidence, limitations, and unknowns.

headline: A Practical Skill Set for Better Coding Agents
lede: This curated collection gives AI coding agents composable habits for TDD, domain modeling, and requirement alignment. Its managed or editable installation keeps the workflow visible, adjustable, and grounded in ordinary engineering practice.

headline: AnyPS5 Translates Console Software Across Platforms
lede: AnyPS5 experiments with a direct route from PlayStation 5 executables to Linux and Windows. Its relinker, PRX implementations, and SPIR-V shader recompiler point toward practical game preservation without distributing proprietary firmware or keys.

headline: A Coding Agent That Gets to the Point
lede: The i-have-adhd skill reshapes coding-assistant replies around the next action, bounded steps, visible progress, and one clear follow-up. It is a small, customizable intervention for developers who need less narration and more movement.

headline: Diagram Design Turns Agent Output Into Visual Language
lede: Diagram Design supplies 29 HTML and SVG templates for producing clean, branded technical graphics inside coding environments. It maps existing colors and fonts to design tokens, and can refine Mermaid or draw.io files without Figma or external dependencies.

headline: Agent Skills Put Engineering Discipline on Rails
lede: These 24 Markdown-based skills give coding agents a repeatable path from specification to implementation, testing, and review. Portable slash commands work across more than 70 agent environments, turning senior-engineering habits into an explicit build plan.

headline: RAD Debugger Rebuilds the Native Debugging Loop
lede: Epic Games’ RAD Debugger pairs a multi-process Windows debugger with a purpose-built representation for debug information and a fast MSVC-compatible linker. The project targets the costly edges of large native codebases: unwieldy binaries, slow links, and difficult inspection.

headline: Claude-Mem Carries Project Context Between Sessions
lede: Claude-Mem captures agent activity, summarizes it semantically, and retrieves the relevant history when work resumes. SQLite storage, Chroma search, progressive disclosure, citations, and privacy exclusions form a local-first memory pipeline for long-running projects.

headline: cmux Gives Parallel Agents a Native Mac Workspace
lede: cmux organizes concurrent coding sessions with vertical tabs, split panes, Git-aware context, notifications, and session restoration. Built with Swift, AppKit, and GPU-accelerated libghostty, it makes a crowded agent workflow feel like a deliberate night desk.

headline: Cua Builds the Cross-Platform Desktop for Agents
lede: Cua provides the operational layer for computer-use agents across Linux, macOS, and Windows. Its fleets, drivers, virtual machines, and benchmarks give developers reproducible environments for screenshots, commands, interface actions, training trajectories, and evaluation.
